SENDS EYES OVER
A RURAL COUNTY

stories.caption:
MISSION BRIEF // F10 LIGHTRUNNER

//Skydio

📍San Mateo, CA

Tech: Autonomous flight

Platform: Fixed-wing drone

Goal: Give responders a live aerial view over long distances, where quadcopters cannot reach.

Why: Skydio says a single MegaDock with the F10's 30-mile flight radius covers nearly 3,000 square miles from one launch location.

Private company → Backers: Not stated in source.

Traction: Concept only. Skydio says F10 deploys to customers in 2027, per Skydio.

Skydio's F10 Lightrunner is a fixed-wing aircraft built for emergency response, search and rescue, and asset inspection missions measured in miles. The company says it launches and catches itself through a robotic takeoff and landing system, and that MegaDock can house up to five F10s.

Skydio introduced F10 at its Ascend 2026 event alongside Controller 2, two new command software platforms, and updates to the existing fleet. Skydio says the F10 is designed to fly at speeds up to 100 mph and to keep working in significant wind, at night and in moderate rain.

Skydio says customers can talk to sales now to get in line for F10 deliveries in 2027.

Source: Skydio, Sept. 24, 2026

Image: skydio.com (courtesy)

MISSION BRIEF // VAMPIRE / L3HARRIS

//L3Harris

📍Melbourne, FL

Tech: Precision strike, ISR

Platform: Self-contained weapons system

Goal: Counter drones and remotely piloted platforms in littoral environments.

Why: It adds a self-contained strike option to the Navy's counter-drone defenses.

Ticker: NYSE: LHX

Traction: Selected by the U.S. Navy to deliver VAMPIRE systems, per L3Harris. Also being delivered to the U.S. Army.

L3Harris describes VAMPIRE as a self-contained weapons solution that offers reconnaissance and precision strike against drones and remotely piloted platforms across domains. The company says it is ruggedizing the system for maritime environments.

The company also unveiled Wraith Shield software earlier this year, which it says can be combined with VAMPIRE and Drone Guardian for layered defense.

Source: L3Harris Technologies, 08SEP26

fields.headline: PARAVISION WINS UP TO $6.5M STATE CONTRACT
fields.deck: The award covers digital identity assurance, but public records do not name the products bought.

stories.caption:
The U.S. State Department has awarded facial recognition developer Paravision a firm-fixed-price contract worth up to $6.5 million, according to federal procurement records that describe the work as "digital detection/identity assurance."

Paravision received the contract on September 23 with an initial obligation of $1.3 million. The contract can run through September 22, 2031. The department competed the work under simplified acquisition procedures as a total small-business set-aside, and it drew a single offer.

Public award records do not name the Paravision products purchased. The description overlaps with technology the company markets to detect manipulated and AI-generated faces, including its deepfake detection product, but the public record does not show whether the award includes deepfake detection, liveness detection, facial recognition or other software. The contract is also much larger than a separate $24,717 purchase order the department placed with Paravision on April 30 for a "purchase card for software license," which records do not tie to the September award.

Source: Biometric Update, October 17, 2026

Image: Biometric Update (courtesy)

fields.benefit_headline:
SOLAR BOATS HOLD
WATCH FOR MONTHS

stories.caption:
MISSION BRIEF // LIGHTFISH

//Seasats

📍San Diego, CA

Tech: Autonomous surveillance

Platform: Unmanned surface vessel

Goal: Detect illegal maritime activity, including drug trafficking and unauthorized vessel entry, across U.S. waters.

Why: The vessels are solar powered, can stay on station for multi-month periods, and can be launched by two people from a boat ramp or pickup truck.

Backers: Shield Capital, L3Harris Technologies, Konvoy Ventures

Traction: Lightfish vessels operating on the Rio Grande since January 2026, with a Gulf of America deployment announced Oct. 2, 2026, per Seasats.

Seasats has put a fleet of Lightfish unmanned surface vessels to sea in the Gulf of America for border surveillance. The boats launch from the Texas coast and are designed to patrol without a crew, watching for drug smuggling and unauthorized vessel traffic.

The work extends earlier Lightfish missions on the Rio Grande, which began in January 2026. The company says the boats are meant to fill gaps left by crewed aircraft and patrol boats, which are limited by crew endurance, operating cost and how much area one asset can cover.

Each vessel carries a modular payload bay that has held electro-optical and infrared cameras, signals payloads and sonar on earlier missions. Seasats CEO Mike Flanigan said a fleet working together can give continuous coverage of an area previously seen only in snapshots.

Source: Seasats via PR Newswire, Oct. 2, 2026

stories.caption:
MISSION BRIEF // COYOTE BLOCK 2C+RM

//Raytheon

📍Tucson, AZ

Tech: Counter-drone interceptor

Platform: Interceptor with tactical rocket motor

Goal: Defeat current and emerging drone threats for U.S. military counter-drone missions.

Why: A rocket motor is intended to speed launch and flight, improving threat engagement times and allowing faster successive shots.

Private company → Backers: Not disclosed in source.

Traction: Three Raytheon-funded developmental tests completed, including first launches of a Coyote effector equipped with a tactical rocket motor, per Raytheon.

Raytheon says the Coyote Block 2C+RM upgrade builds on current Coyote variants, which have intercepted hundreds of drones in combat. The design uses a common backbone so the Coyote family can scale across counter-drone missions. The upgrade adds a new seeker and warhead.

Source: RTX, 12OCT26
